**p12:** Passing is right. Forbidden Lance would only cut the damage from 900 to 100, and Condemned Witch dies either way. The Lance is worth more as a Set protection card.

**p01:** Only Dark Rebellion (option 5) wins this turn. Fiendish Chain stops Honest from attacking, so going straight to battle (B) deals only 1400 of the 2050 needed.

**p06:** Ritual Summoning Sauravis with Djinn Demolisher and Honest (C) is the strongest play. Discarding SDQ first (A) also works, because the other SDQ effect can still be used afterwards.

positions.assessment: Chronocorder (1000) attacks Condemned Witch (100). Putting Lance on Chronocorder still loses the Witch, and only cuts the damage from 900 to 100. The Witch is DARK, so Honest can't help. Spending the Lance to save 800 LP at 8000 LP is poor value. Kept Set, it can protect Saffira or win a battle later. Passing is right.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: Correct: the Witch dies whatever you do, so the Lance would only save 800 LP. It's worth more held for protection or a battle.

positions.assessment: Opponent is at 2050 LP with no monsters and no Set cards. Fiendish Chain on Honest means it can't attack, so a plain Battle Phase only gets Geargiaccelerator's 1400 through. Overlaying Honest and the stolen Geargiaccelerator into Dark Rebellion (2500) gives a lethal direct attack. It also sends the Chain to the GY and keeps the stolen monster from going back to the opponent. That is the winning line.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: Finds the lethal: 2500 direct beats 2050, and it clears both the Chain and the stolen monster.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: Misreads Fiendish Chain, which stops Honest from attacking. Only 1400 damage gets through, so a lethal turn is thrown away and Geargiaccelerator goes back to the opponent.

positions.assessment: In Main Phase 2 the opponent is at 2900 LP with 6 cards, including a known Blue-Eyes Alternative (it destroys a targeted monster). Both SDQ effects are still unused this turn, and either one sends a LIGHT monster from hand to the GY, which turns on Saffira's End Phase effect. Banishing SDQ from the GY to Ritual Summon Sauravis with Demolisher + Honest gives an untargetable 2600 body that can also negate Special Summons. That shuts out the Alternative, sets up lethal next turn, and switches on Saffira's End Phase effect. The hand-discard SDQ effect is also good and doesn't block the summon. Pre-Preparation adds redundant cards to an already overfull hand (8, so you'll discard at End Phase).

grades.label: A
grades.reason: Turns on Saffira's End Phase effect and keeps SDQ's GY effect available. Sound, but the reason doesn't mention building the board, which C does.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: Adds redundant cards to an 8-card hand that will have to discard down at End Phase. It doesn't develop the board against Blue-Eyes or turn on Saffira's End Phase effect by itself.

grades.label: C
grades.reason: Legal and strong: Demolisher makes Sauravis untargetable by the Alternative, Sauravis can negate their Special Summons, and Tributing Honest from hand turns on Saffira's End Phase effect. The board threatens lethal next turn.
